basis: Craniosynostosis, structural ocular abnormalities and developmental impairment characterize the syndrome; cardiac defect frequencies are unclear.
Adenoma originates in the adrenal cortex; absence of hormone secretion does not change its endocrine gland origin.
Skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability, symblepharon and numerous cutaneous nevi each occur in 30-79%.
Childhood autoinflammatory periodic fever syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish lasting organ damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across chromosome 11 partial duplications; other malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Immunodeficiency with cytopenias and hemophagocytosis; hepatitis in 8/9 and jejunoileal ulceration in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed Crohn disease is not the basis.
Listeria infection; direct CNS infection and meningitis are annotated in 30-79%. Bacteremia does not establish blood-cell damage.
Corneal degeneration and deafness are the defining manifestations.
Ischemic injury of the optic nerve, which belongs to the ocular axis; systemic vascular disease is not intrinsic to this diagnosis.
Multifocal glomus-cell vascular proliferation typically involving skin and subcutis; no common additional organ damage established.
Congenital erythroid marrow failure defines the disease; specific skeletal, cardiac, renal and neurologic abnormalities are generally below 30%.
Developmental impairment, epilepsy and structural brain abnormalities define ACTL6B encephalopathy; feeding difficulty and central hypotonia add no organ axis.
Hydrocephalus, intellectual disability and spasticity define the neurologic disorder; characteristic adducted thumbs reflect congenital thumb muscle abnormalities.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction defines disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation is characteristic of PCD and reported in 1/1 annotated patient.
Regenerative nodules occupy hepatic parenchyma; portal hypertension occurs in 5-29%. Associated immune and hematologic disorders are separate conditions.
Developmental delay in 24/24 defines disease; nail dysplasia in 8/24 (~33%). Individual renal and cardiac defects are below 30%; overlap is unspecified.
Marrow failure; absent thumbs 3/3, renal agenesis 3/4 and hydrocephalus 3/4. Anal atresia 2/3 and cardiac/endocrine anomalies omitted by the four-axis cap.
Childhood malignant tumor originating in the cerebellum.
Metabolic crises with lactic acidosis, neurologic regression and intrinsic mitochondrial myopathy define the disorder.
Ventricular arrhythmia defines disease; intrinsic proximal skeletal muscle weakness occurs in 1/3 (~33%), meeting the threshold in a small cohort.
Autoimmune cutaneous dermatomyositis without clinical muscle weakness; interstitial lung disease affects roughly 30-50%, varying by population and antibody status.
IgG4-mediated infiltration of lacrimal and salivary glands defines disease; renal and other systemic manifestations are uncommon or separately diagnosed.
Histoplasma-associated inflammation of the pericardium; common additional organ damage is not established for this specific concept.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome; kidney dysplasia, anophthalmia and camptodactyly each occur in 30-79%. Specific cardiac defects are annotated at 5-29%.
Rickettsia africae infection; necrotic inoculation eschars directly damage skin in approximately 80-90%, unlike a transient generalized rash.
